item.title: A whole stand at a tennis match filming on phones, and one person recording in Meta glasses while still watching the game.
item.dc:creator: ShikshanNivesh
item.content:encoded:
A whole stand at a tennis match filming on phones, and one person recording in Meta glasses while still watching the game. Every one of those phones was designed before AI. My theory is that Meta ($META) is eventually going after Apple ($AAPL) and Samsung with this.
Mark Zuckerberg said something close to this on Meta's results call in January. He compared AI glasses today to the moment smartphones arrived. It was only a matter of time, he said, until every flip phone became a smartphone. He also said sales of Meta's glasses more than tripled in 2025. It will not happen soon, because Apple has more than 2.5 billion active devices and about $146 billion in cash and securities. But people using their phones less is exactly what Meta is building for.

item.title: Well, I’m testing CoreCLR right now with Unity 7 Alpha!
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
Well, I’m testing CoreCLR right now with Unity 7 Alpha!
Below are the steps to enable it, but looks like it is set by default in Unity 7 Alpha.
Edit → Project Settings → Player → Other Settings → Configuration → Scripting Backend → CoreCLR.
📌 Here're a few great things about it:
- Modern JIT compiler to optimize C# execution. - Generational garbage collection for managing memory. - Better debugging with standard .NET tools. - .NET 10 and C# 14 support planned for future updates.
📊 Few community benchmarks with Unity 6.7’s experimental desktop player (from Unity forums):
- C# CPU path tracing, single thread: 17.1× speedup vs Mono and 2.49× vs IL2CPP. - C# CPU path tracing, multiple threads: 17.85× speedup vs Mono and 2.81× vs IL2CPP. - Boat Attack: ~10% lower average frame time vs Mono in a quick single-run test. - Happy Harvest: ~15% lower average frame time vs Mono in a quick single-run test.
In summary: It’s supposed to be very, very fast when you hit Play in Unity. I’m testing that right now with the Meta XR SDKs!

item.title: About a year and a half ago, I built a few demos with microgestures, and they’re extremely relevant now with Meta VR Glasses! These are s...
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
About a year and a half ago, I built a few demos with microgestures, and they’re extremely relevant now with Meta VR Glasses! These are small, low-effort thumb movements that let you trigger actions, navigate content, and even move through VR without controllers or large hand movements. 🙌
- Thumb tap and double tap for contextual actions and shortcuts
- Swipe left, right, up, or down for directional input
- Navigate UI and content almost like using a tiny D-pad with your thumb
- Combine microgestures with gaze for low-effort targeting and interactions
- Use them for locomotion, paging, media controls, teleportation, and other contextual actions
